questions.question: If the sum of three consecutive odd numbers is 111, what is the largest number?
questions.solution:
Let the three consecutive odd numbers be x, x + 2, and x + 4.

The sum of these numbers is given as 111.

x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) = 111

3x + 6 = 111

3x = 111 − 6

3x = 105

x = 105 ÷ 3

x = 35

First odd number (x) = 35

Second odd number (x + 2) = 37

Third odd number (x + 4) = 39

Comparing the three numbers 35, 37, and 39, the largest number is 39.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 4**”.

questions.question: Who appoints the Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 75** of the **Indian Constitution**, the **Prime Minister** is appointed by the **President of India**. While the President makes the formal appointment, they are bound by constitutional conventions to appoint the leader of the party or coalition that commands a **majority** in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• The **President** also appoints other **Ministers** of the Union, but this is done specifically on the **advice** of the Prime Minister.
 
• The Prime Minister serves as the **Head of the Government** and the chief link between the **Cabinet** and the President. Although the Prime Minister holds office during the **pleasure of the President**, they cannot be dismissed as long as they maintain a majority in the Lower House.
 
• Before the Prime Minister enters office, the **President** administers the **oaths of office and secrecy** as per the forms set out in the **Third Schedule** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliament**:

 
 
• Comprises the **President**, the **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States), and the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People). While it is the legislative body, it does not formally appoint the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of India**:
 
 
• The head of the **Judiciary** and the **Supreme Court**. The Chief Justice administers the oath of office to the **President** under **Article 60**, but has no role in the executive appointment of the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Vice President**:
 
 
• Functions as the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha**. According to **Article 65**, the Vice President acts as President only during casual vacancies or the President's absence.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility**:
 
 
• A person must be a member of either house of Parliament to be Prime Minister. If not a member at the time of appointment, they must be elected to either the **Lok Sabha** or **Rajya Sabha** within **six months**.

questions.question: Which article allows Parliament to amend the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 368**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 368**, located in **Part XX** of the **Constitution of India**, defines the power of **Parliament** to amend the Constitution and provides the specific procedure for such modifications.
 
• The **Parliament** may, in the exercise of its constituent power, amend by way of addition, variation, or repeal any provision of the Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down.
 
• An amendment of the Constitution can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill for the purpose in either **House of Parliament** (**Lok Sabha** or **Rajya Sabha**) and not in the **State Legislatures**.
 
• The Bill must be passed in each House by a **Special Majority**, which requires a majority of the total membership of that House and a majority of not less than **two-thirds** of the members of that House present and voting.
 
• The **Supreme Court**, in the historic **Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)**, ruled that **Parliament** cannot amend those provisions which form the **Basic Structure** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 352**

 
 
• Relates to the proclamation of a **National Emergency** by the **President** when the security of India is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
 
 
• **Article 356**
 
 
• Commonly known as **President’s Rule**, it allows for the suspension of state government and the imposition of direct central government rule in a state if the constitutional machinery fails.
 
 
 
• **Article 370**
 
 
• Formerly granted a **Temporary Special Status** to the state of **Jammu and Kashmir**; its primary provisions were rendered inoperative by a Presidential Order in **August 2019**.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the Giddha dance?

options.text: A women's folk dance involving rhythmic clapping and singing
A solo dance performed by men

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A women's folk dance involving rhythmic clapping and singing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Giddha** is a popular and **vibrant folk dance** originating from the **Punjab** region of **India** and **Pakistan**, performed exclusively by **women**.
 
• The dance is highly **rhythmic** and is characterized by its lack of heavy instrumentation; instead, the **beat** is primarily generated through **rhythmic clapping** and the use of a **Dhol** (barrel drum).
 
• It is often considered the female counterpart to the male-centric **Bhangra** dance, sharing similar energy levels but emphasizing **grace**, **femininity**, and **storytelling**.
 
• The performance involves women standing in a **circle** while singing **Boliyaan**, which are traditional **couplets** or short folk songs that reflect the **daily lives**, **emotions**, and **social experiences** of Punjabi women.
 
• One or two women usually step into the center of the circle to perform the **main dance steps** while the others provide the **chorus** and **clapping** support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cultural Significance and Occasions**:

 
 
• **Giddha** is typically performed during **festivals** such as **Baisakhi** (harvest festival) and **Teeyan** (monsoon festival dedicated to women).
 
• It is also a staple at **weddings** and other family celebrations, serving as a medium for **social bonding** and **merriment**.
 
 
 
• **Attire and Ornamentation**:
 
 
• Performers wear bright, colorful **Salwar Kameez** or **Lehengas** made of **silk** or **satin**, often heavily embroidered with **Gota-patti** or **Phulkari** work.
 
• Specific traditional **jewelry** includes the **Saggi Phul** (a floral-shaped head ornament), **Tikka**, and heavy **bangles** that add to the visual and auditory spectacle of the dance.
 
 
 
• **Thematic Content of Boliyaan**:
 
 
• The lyrics often humorously address **familial relationships**, such as the bond between a **mother-in-law** and **daughter-in-law**, or celebrate **romantic love** and **nature**.

questions.question: Which mountain range is considered the oldest in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aravalli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aravalli Range** is geologically recognized as the **oldest fold mountain** system in India and is among the oldest in the world.
 
• It originated during the **Precambrian Era**, specifically the **Proterozoic Eon**, approximately **1.8 billion years** ago, as part of the **Aravalli-Delhi Orogeny**.
 
• Today, it is categorized as a **relict mountain** or **residual mountain** because its once-towering peaks have been significantly lowered by millions of years of **weathering** and **erosion**.
 
• The range extends for about **800 kilometers** in a **Southwest-Northeast** direction, covering parts of **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, **Haryana**, and **Delhi**.
 
• The highest peak of the Aravalli range is **Guru Shikhar**, located in **Mount Abu**, reaching an elevation of **1,722 meters** above sea level.
 
• The range acts as a **climatic barrier**, preventing the eastward expansion of the **Thar Desert** and influencing the rainfall patterns in Northwest India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayas**:

 
 
• These are **Young Fold Mountains** formed during the **Cenozoic Era** (Tertiary Period) due to the collision between the **Indian Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate**.
 
• They are characterized by **high peaks**, **deep valleys**, and **fast-flowing rivers**, and they are still geologically **active** and growing.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats**:
 
 
• Also known as **Sahyadri**, this range runs parallel to the **western coast** and is older than the Himalayas but younger than the Aravallis.
 
• They represent the **faulted edge** of the **Deccan Plateau** and are a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** known for immense **biodiversity**.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Ghats**:
 
 
• A discontinuous range of mountains along India's **eastern coast** that has been eroded by major peninsular rivers like the **Godavari** and **Krishna**.

questions.question: Which celestial phenomenon results from the Earth blocking the Sun's light from reaching the Moon?

• A **Lunar eclipse** occurs specifically when the **Earth** passes directly between the **Sun** and the **Moon**, obstructing the solar rays from illuminating the lunar surface.
 
• This celestial alignment results in the Earth casting its **shadow** on the Moon, which is divided into the **Umbra** (the darkest central part) and the **Penumbra** (the outer, lighter part).
 
• This phenomenon is only possible during the **Full Moon** phase, as the Sun and Moon must be at opposite points relative to the Earth.
 
• During a **Total Lunar Eclipse**, the Moon often appears reddish because the Earth's atmosphere scatters shorter wavelengths (blue) and refracts longer wavelengths (red) toward the Moon, a process known as **Rayleigh scattering**.
 
• Unlike solar eclipses, a lunar eclipse can be observed safely with the naked eye and is visible from any location on the **night-side** of the Earth.

• **Meteor shower**:
 
 
• This is a celestial event where multiple **meteors** (shooting stars) are observed to originate from a single point in the sky.
 
• It is caused by the **Earth** passing through a stream of **cosmic debris** or dust left behind by a **comet** or asteroid.
 
 
 
• **Aurora borealis**:

questions.question: Cardiac muscles are classified as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Involuntary muscles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cardiac muscles** are a specialized type of muscle tissue found exclusively in the **myocardium**, which is the middle layer of the **heart** wall.
 
• These muscles are classified as **involuntary muscles** because their rhythmic contraction and relaxation occur automatically and are not under the conscious control of the **somatic nervous system**.
 
• The primary function of cardiac muscle is to pump blood throughout the **circulatory system** by contracting the heart chambers.
 
• Unlike skeletal muscles, cardiac muscles are **myogenic**, meaning the impulse for contraction originates within the muscle tissue itself via the **Sinoatrial (SA) node**, although the **autonomic nervous system** can modulate the heart rate.
 
• Structurally, cardiac muscle cells are **branched**, **uninucleated**, and contain **striations** (bands of actin and myosin), but their functional classification remains involuntary due to the lack of conscious regulation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Voluntary muscles**:

 
 
• These are primarily **skeletal muscles** attached to the **bones**.
 
• They are controlled by the **will** of the individual through the **central nervous system** for movement and posture.
 
 
 
• **Smooth muscles**:
 
 
• These are **non-striated**, spindle-shaped muscles found in the walls of hollow internal organs like the **stomach**, **intestines**, and **blood vessels**.
 
• Like cardiac muscles, they are **involuntary**, but they lack the striations and branching characteristic of the heart muscle.
 
 
 
• **Striated skeletal muscles**:
 
 
• These are **long**, **cylindrical**, and **unbranched** fibers that appear striped under a microscope.
 
• They are distinguished from cardiac muscles by being **multinucleated** and strictly **voluntary** in nature.
 
 
 
• **Intercalated Discs**:
 
 
• A unique feature of **cardiac muscle** is the presence of **intercalated discs** which contain **gap junctions**.
 
• These structures allow for rapid **electrical communication** between cells, ensuring the heart contracts as a single functional unit called a **syncytium**.

Perform calculations using the **BODMAS** order: Brackets, Of, Division, Addition/Subtraction.

Solve **36 ÷ 3 = 12** and **28 of 1 = 28**.

Substitute back: **93 − 47 + 19 + 12 + 28 − 21**.

Combine positive terms: **93 + 19 + 12 + 28 = 152**.

Combine negative terms: **−47 − 21 = −68**.

Final result: **152 − 68 = 84**.

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

questions.question: sqrt{(0.0225)/(0.04)} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify **perfect squares**: 225 is 15² and 4 is 2².

Equalize decimal places inside the root: √(0.0225 ÷ 0.0400).

Remove decimals: √(225 ÷ 400) = 15 ÷ 20.

Simplify: 15 ÷ 20 = 0.75.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** √(0.0225 ÷ 0.04)

**Method:** Convert decimals to **fractions** to simplify the square root expression.

⇒ √((225 ÷ 10000) ÷ (4 ÷ 100))

⇒ √((225 ÷ 10000) × (100 ÷ 4))

⇒ √(225 ÷ 400)

⇒ √225 ÷ √400

⇒ 15 ÷ 20

⇒ 3 ÷ 4

⇒ 0.75

**∴ The correct answer is 0.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Decimals

The **square root** of a decimal with 'n' decimal places will always result in a number with 'n/2' decimal places, provided the digits form a perfect square.

Division of Decimals

When dividing decimals, it is easier to **multiply** both the numerator and denominator by a power of 10 (like 100 or 10000) to remove the decimal points before calculation.

Perfect Squares to Remember

Memorizing **squares** up to 25 (e.g., 15² = 225, 25² = 625) significantly speeds up simplification and root-finding tasks.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the expression as the **algebraic identity**: a² + b² + 2ab = (a + b)².

Let **a = 4.10** and **b = 1.90**.

Verify the middle term: 2 × a × b = 2 × 4.10 × 1.90 = 2 × 7.79 = **15.58**.

Expression = (4.10 + 1.90)² = (6.00)² = **36.00**.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.00.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 4.10 × 4.10 + 1.90 × 1.90 + 15.58

**Method:** Perform **multiplication** and **addition** as per **BODMAS** rules.

⇒ (4.10 × 4.10) + (1.90 × 1.90) + 15.58

⇒ 16.81 + 3.61 + 15.58

⇒ 20.42 + 15.58

⇒ 36.00

**∴ The correct answer is 36.00.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² are fundamental expansion rules.

BODMAS Rule

The order of operations: **Brackets**, **Orders**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b), which is useful for simplifying products of numbers centered around a mean.

questions.question: The area of a rhombus is 180 square cm. One of the diagonal is 20 cm. What is the ratio of the two diagonals?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of diagonals = 2 × **Area**

20 × d₂ = 2 × 180

d₂ = 360 ÷ 20 = 18 cm

**Ratio** = 20 : 18 = 10 : 9

**∴ The correct answer is 10 : 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b97edfc65b6e3f482626aad39ab3277ee953ff22dd7bcf41c820d91ef6e9b418.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ **Area** of rhombus = 180 cm²

⇒ First **Diagonal** (d₁) = 20 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ 180 = (1/2) × 20 × d₂

⇒ 180 = 10 × d₂

⇒ d₂ = 180 ÷ 10 = 18 cm

⇒ Required **Ratio** = d₁ : d₂

⇒ Ratio = 20 : 18 = 10 : 9

**∴ The correct answer is 10 : 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Side of Rhombus

The side 'a' of a rhombus can be calculated using diagonals: a = (1/2) × √(d₁² + d₂²).

Perimeter of Rhombus

Since all sides are equal, the perimeter is given by 4 × side.

Diagonal Properties

The diagonals of a rhombus always bisect each other at right angles (90°).

questions.question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 100 cm. One of the diagonal is 30 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the other diagonal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **side** of the **rhombus** = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm.

The half of the given **diagonal** = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm.

Since diagonals bisect at **90°**, we use the **Pythagorean triple** (3, 4, 5) scaled by 5: (15, 20, 25).

The other half-diagonal is 20 cm.

The total length of the **other diagonal** = 20 × 2 = 40 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** = 100 cm and **Diagonal (d₁)** = 30 cm.

**Formula Used:**

1. Side (a) = Perimeter ÷ 4

2. a² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d1c77a7ed49eacdbe4b2ba7a2bd519715d7f89a55fd4fe54724f1f10c2cb9a98.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Side (a) = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm

⇒ Half of first diagonal = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm

⇒ Let the other half diagonal be x.

⇒ In **right-angled triangle** AOB: AO² + OB² = AB²

⇒ 15² + x² = 25²

⇒ 225 + x² = 625

⇒ x² = 625 − 225

⇒ x² = 400

⇒ x = √400 = 20 cm

⇒ Length of other diagonal (d₂) = 2 × x = 2 × 20 = 40 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 40 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rhombus

The area can be calculated using diagonals: Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂.

Relationship between Side and Diagonals

The formula relating side (a) and diagonals is: 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Diagonals Property

In a rhombus, diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°) and also bisect the vertex angles.

questions.question: Least Common Multiple of A and B is 36 and C = 24. What is the Least Common Multiple of A, B and C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of three numbers, we use the property: **LCM(A, B, C) = LCM(LCM(A, B), C)**.

Given **LCM(A, B) = 36** and **C = 24**.

We simply need to find **LCM(36, 24)**.

List multiples of the larger number (36): 36, 72...

Since 72 is exactly divisible by 24 (24 × 3 = 72), the **LCM is 72**.

**∴ The correct answer is 72.**

questions.question: The Highest Common Factor of the two numbers is 12. Which of the following can be the Least Common Multiple of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of any set of numbers must always be exactly **divisible** by their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**.

Given **HCF** = 12, we check which option is a multiple of 12.

144 ÷ 12 = 12 (Remains 0).

Since 144 is the only option divisible by 12, it can be the **LCM**.

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**HCF** of two numbers = 12

**Property Used:**

If two numbers are 12x and 12y (where x and y are **coprime**), then their **LCM** = 12 × x × y.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff740b8d8f2ed9ac3d0e330dd81426177818dd35cd236cccfed8a7697c089480.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the numbers be a and b.

⇒ a = 12p and b = 12q (where p, q are integers).

⇒ **LCM**(a, b) = 12 × LCM(p, q).

⇒ This implies **LCM** must be divisible by 12.

⇒ Option 1: 130 ÷ 12 = 10.83 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 2: 110 ÷ 12 = 9.16 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 3: 144 ÷ 12 = 12 (Integer)

⇒ Option 4: 95 ÷ 12 = 7.91 (Not an integer)

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

HCF of Coprime Numbers

If two numbers are **coprime**, their **Highest Common Factor** is always 1, and their **LCM** is simply the product of the two numbers.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators). LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).

questions.question: A is 30 percent less than B. If value of A is 630, then what is the value of B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**A** is 30% less than **B**, which means **A** is 70% of **B**.

70% of **B** = 630

100% of **B** = (630 ÷ 70) × 100

Value of **B** = 9 × 100 = 900

**∴ The correct answer is 900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Value of **A** = 630

Relationship: **A** = **B** − 30% of **B**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa781db64ff9c076efa8c81d7b2300e17d5ab8304d56409dec0d04ddab904bf7.png] 

**Formula used:**

Value = Base × (100 − % Decrease) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ 630 = **B** × (100 − 30) ÷ 100

⇒ 630 = **B** × (70 ÷ 100)

⇒ 630 = **B** × 0.7

⇒ **B** = 630 ÷ 0.7

⇒ **B** = 900

**∴ The correct answer is 900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100.

Base Comparison Rule

If **A** is x% less than **B**, then **B** is [x ÷ (100 − x)] × 100% more than **A**.

Multiplier Method

A 30% decrease corresponds to a multiplying factor of 0.70, while a 30% increase corresponds to 1.30.

questions.question: A is (1/4) of B. A is how much percent less than B?

The difference between B and A is 4 − 1 = 3 units.

Percentage less = (Difference / Base value B) × 100.

⇒ (3 / 4) × 100 = 75%.

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

**Calculations:**

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change is calculated as [|New Value − Old Value| / Old Value] × 100. The denominator is always the **reference (base) value**.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Common fractions like 1/4 = 25%, 1/2 = 50%, and 3/4 = 75% are helpful for quick **quantitative aptitude** calculations.

Base Value Rule

In the phrase 'A is less than B', **B** is the base value. In 'B is more than A', **A** becomes the base value.

questions.question: The ratio of two number A and B is 7 : 5. If both numbers are increased by 3, then the ratio of A and B becomes 4 : 3. What is the sum of initial values of A and B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial **Ratio** A : B = 7 : 5 (Difference = 2 parts)

New **Ratio** A : B = 4 : 3 (Difference = 1 part)

Multiply new ratio by 2 to equate difference: 8 : 6

Increase in each part = 8 − 7 = 1 unit → 3

Sum of initial parts = 7 + 5 = 12 units

Total **Initial Sum** = 12 × 3 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given **initial ratio** of **Numbers** A and B is 7 : 5.

Let the common multiplier be x. So, A = 7x and B = 5x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7886dc46983e445873c1ca8b3807581253392e47785b311bab16b52a8fe5ff91.png] 

According to the question, when both numbers are **increased** by 3:

⇒ (7x + 3) / (5x + 3) = 4 / 3

⇒ 3 × (7x + 3) = 4 × (5x + 3)

⇒ 21x + 9 = 20x + 12

⇒ 21x − 20x = 12 − 9

⇒ x = 3

**Initial Values**:

⇒ A = 7 × 3 = 21

⇒ B = 5 × 3 = 15

⇒ **Sum** of A and B = 21 + 15 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Balancing Method

When the same value is added or subtracted from both terms, the difference between the terms remains proportional. Equating the differences simplifies calculation.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios (a : b) and (c : d) is (ac : bd), obtained by multiplying corresponding terms.

Duplicate and Triplicate Ratios

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a² : b², and the triplicate ratio is a³ : b³.

Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
Had the technical errors been corrected by the software team before the product launch?

options.text: Did the software team correct the technical errors before the product launch?

Has the software team corrected the technical errors before the product launch?
Was the software team correcting the technical errors before the product launch?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Had the software team corrected the technical errors before the product launch?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the **Past Perfect Tense** in its **Interrogative Form**. The passive structure for this tense is: **Had + Object + been + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject?**

• To transform this into the **Active Voice**, the **Agent** of the action (**the software team**) must move to the subject position, and the **Recipient** of the action (**the technical errors**) must move to the object position.

• The **Active Voice** structure for an interrogative sentence in the **Past Perfect Tense** is: **Had + Subject + V3 (Past Participle) + Object?**

• In this conversion, the auxiliary **been** is removed as it is only a marker for the passive construction. The main verb **corrected** remains in its **Past Participle (V3)** form.

• The resulting sentence, **Had the software team corrected the technical errors before the product launch?**, maintains the same **chronological sequence** and **tense consistency** as the original question.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Grammatical Tense Analysis**:

• **Simple Past (Did)**: Used for actions that were completed at a specific time in the past. Using **did** would require the base form of the verb **correct**, which changes the tense of the original query.

• **Present Perfect (Has/Have)**: Connects a past action to the present moment. Using **has** would be grammatically incorrect because the original context is set entirely in the past before a **product launch**.

• **Past Continuous (Was/Were + V-ing)**: Focuses on the duration or ongoing nature of a past action. This changes the **aspect** from a completed action (perfect) to an ongoing one (continuous).

• **Past Perfect Usage**: Specifically used to emphasize that one action was completed before another action or point in the past (the **product launch**).

</ul

Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The injured man must be taken to the hospital at once.

• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice**. This is identified by the structure: **Subject (The injured man)** + **Modal Verb (must)** + **be** + **Past Participle (taken)**.

• When a passive sentence expresses an **urgent command**, **advice**, or **instruction** and does not mention a specific **agent** (the doer of the action), it is commonly converted into the **Active Voice** using the **Imperative Mood**.

• **Active Voice:** The subject performs the action (e.g., **'Take the man'**). It is direct and clear.

• **Option 2:** This incorrectly identifies the **hospital** as the **agent** (the one doing the taking/carrying), whereas the hospital is actually the **destination**.

• **Option 4:** This uses the **'Let + Object + be + V3'** structure, which is another way to form the **Passive Voice** for imperative sentences. It does not fulfill the requirement for **Active Voice**.

</ul

__

• The phrase **'none uncommon'** used in the original sentence is grammatically incorrect because **'none'** is a pronoun or an adverb meaning **'not any'** or **'to no extent'**, and it cannot properly modify the adjective **'uncommon'** in this specific sentence structure.

• The correct expression **'not uncommon'** is a rhetorical device known as **litotes**, where a negative statement (not) is used to affirm a positive sentiment (common); it suggests that the event occurs with reasonable **frequency**.

• In the structure **'It is'** (contracted as **'It's'**), the word **'is'** acts as a **linking verb** which must be followed by an adjective or an **adjectival phrase**; the adverb **'not'** is the standard tool for negating such adjectives in English.

• The term **'street musicians'** is a correctly formed **compound noun** referring to individuals who perform music in public spaces for tips, fitting the context of the sentence perfectly.

• **'Nothing uncommon'** vs. **'Not uncommon'**:

• **'Nothing'** is a **pronoun**. While one could say **'There is nothing uncommon about this'**, it does not fit the **dummy subject** structure of **'It is...'** as effectively as the adverb **'not'**.

• **'Never uncommon'** and **'Streets of musicians'**:

• **'Never'** is an **adverb of frequency** meaning **'at no time'**; using it here would create an absolute statement that is stylistically unusual for describing a casual weekend observation.

• The phrase **'streets of musicians'** uses a **prepositional phrase** that changes the meaning entirely, suggesting the physical roads are populated by or belong to musicians, rather than describing the **buskers** themselves.

• **Litotes in English**:

• This figure of speech is frequently used in **formal writing** and **literature** to provide **emphasis** through understatement, often making a claim seem more objective or cautious.
